mainTopic: The greatness and rewards of צדקה, with a story about the nickname of a Sage and the source that a מצורע in his counting days makes a person impure.
overview: The גמרא teaches that every small coin of צדקה joins into one big total, like scales in a coat of mail or threads in a garment. It then tells why the Sage who reported this was nicknamed 'the infant who perverted the ways of his mother'. רב אחדבוי בר אמי mockingly took apart רב ששת's proof that a מצורע in his counting days makes a person impure. רב אחדבוי was punished until his mother, who had nursed רב ששת, pleaded for him. The גמרא then gives the real source for that rule: a גזירה שוה from רבי שמעון בן יוחי. Back on צדקה, רבי אלעזר says secret giving is greater than משה רבינו, and רבי יצחק reads the same פסוק differently. רבי יצחק adds that giving a פרוטה earns six blessings and comforting the poor earns eleven, and that הקב״ה gives the pursuer of צדקה money to give, while רב נחמן בר יצחק says He sends him worthy recipients. The עמוד ends with רבי יהושע בן לוי's teaching that regular givers merit wise, wealthy, and learned sons, and the first proof continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Every coin of charity joins into one big coat of mail
steps.stepSummary: Quoting רבי אלעזר, a Sage nicknamed 'the infant who perverted the ways of his mother' explains the פסוק 'He put on צדקה like a coat of mail': small coins of צדקה add up to a large sum, like small scales forming one coat of armor.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sage called 'who perverted the ways of his mother' said in the name of רבי אלעזר: What does the פסוק 'And He put on charity like a coat of mail' mean? It tells you that just as each small scale of a coat of mail joins with the others to make one big coat of mail, so too each small coin of charity joins with the others to make a big sum.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching of רבי אלעזר: a coat of mail is made of many small scales, and in the same way many small coins of צדקה build up a great total.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that a small donation is not 'nothing'. Each פרוטה counts and joins into one large amount, just as no single scale is armor alone, but together they make full armor.

keyTerms.meaning: A coat of mail (armor made of small scales)
A scale or small plate of the armor

phrases.english: "who perverted the ways of his mother,"
phrases.notes: This is the end of a Sage's nickname that started just before here. The גמרא explains the nickname a few lines down.

phrases.english: said in the name of Rabbi Elazar:
What is meant by that which is written:
"And He put on charity like a coat of mail"?
phrases.notes: ישעיה 59:17

phrases.english: It comes to tell you:
just as this coat of mail:
each and every scale
joins into one large coat of mail,
so too charity:
each and every small coin
joins into a large sum.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section with an aggadic teaching on צדקה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Small gifts of צדקה add up into one great total, like scales forming a coat of mail.

steps.title: A second verse: threads joining into a garment
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא learns the same idea from a different פסוק: just as threads join into a garment, coins of צדקה join into a great sum.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא says the idea comes from here: 'And all our charities are like a stained garment.' Just as each thread joins with the others to make one big garment, so too each small coin of charity joins with the others into a big sum.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא gives a different source for the same lesson: a garment made of many threads.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lesson does not change; only the פסוק and the picture change. Instead of armor scales, רבי חנינא points to threads that together make a full garment.
steps.whatToRemember: Both רבי אלעזר and רבי חנינא teach that every small coin of צדקה counts and joins into a large total. They differ only in which פסוק they use.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina says it is learned from here:
"And all our charities are like a stained garment";
phrases.notes: ישעיה 64:5

phrases.english: just as this garment:
each and every thread
joins into one large garment,
so too charity:
each and every small coin
joins into a large sum.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different פסוק for the same lesson taught in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Coins of צדקה join together like threads in a garment.

steps.title: Why did that Sage get his strange nickname?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pauses to ask why the Sage who reported רבי אלעזר's teaching was called 'the infant who perverted the ways of his mother'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did they call him 'the infant who perverted the ways of his mother'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the topic of צדקה and asks about the nickname from step 1. This question sets up the story that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The nickname sounds harsh, so the גמרא wants to explain where it came from. The answer is a story about a halachic discussion between two Sages.
steps.confusionAlert: עוּלָּא here is not the famous אמורא named עולא. It means 'infant', part of the nickname.

phrases.english: Why did they call him
"the infant who perverted the ways of his mother"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns back to the nickname mentioned in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason behind the Sage's nickname.

steps.title: Does a מצורע in his counting days make a person impure?
steps.stepSummary: The answer to the nickname question begins with a story: רב אחדבוי בר אמי asked רב ששת for the source that a מצורע during his seven counting days makes a person impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was because רב אחדבוי בר אמי asked רב ששת: From where do we know that a מצורע during his counting days makes a person impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts the story behind the nickname. רב אחדבוי asks רב ששת a halachic question about the טומאה of a מצורע in his counting days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מצורע in the middle of his purification still has some טומאה. The question is where the תורה shows that he makes another person impure by touching him.

keyTerms.meaning: A person with צרעת (a kind of skin affliction)
His counting days: the seven days of his purification process

phrases.english: Because he asked

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָדְבוּי בַּר אַמֵּי מֵרַב שֵׁשֶׁת:
phrases.english: Rav Achadvoi bar Ami of Rav Sheshet:
From where do we know about a leper during his counting days,
phrases.notes: These are the seven days between the bird ceremony and his final קרבנות.

phrases.english: that he makes a person impure?

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּבְעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב אַחָדְבוּי בַּר אַמֵּי מֵרַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the story that answers the question in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that a מצורע in his counting days makes a person impure.

steps.title: Since he makes clothes impure, he makes people impure
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers: because the מצורע makes clothes impure, he must make people impure too.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Since he makes clothes impure, he also makes a person impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives a logical source: if the מצורע's clothes become impure, then people he touches become impure too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת uses a general rule: anything that makes clothes impure also makes people impure. He points to the clothes because the תורה tells the מצורע to wash his clothes at the end of his counting days.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Since he makes clothes impure,
he makes a person impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחדבוי's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Whatever makes clothes impure also makes people impure.

steps.title: Maybe clothes attached to him are a special case
steps.stepSummary: רב אחדבוי objects: maybe the clothes are impure only because they are attached to the impure person, and that tells us nothing about other people. He proves it from someone who moves a נבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Maybe impurity through connection is different. After all, a person who moves a carcass makes his clothes impure but does not make another person impure!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחדבוי attacks רב ששת's rule by showing a case where clothes become impure but people do not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The clothes are touching the מצורע while he is impure, so their impurity might come from being connected to him. The case of היסט נבילה shows that 'clothes become impure' does not always mean 'people become impure', so רב ששת's rule is broken.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity through connection: things attached to the impure person
The carcass of an animal that died without proper שחיטה

phrases.english: He said to him:
Perhaps impurity through connection is different,
phrases.notes: He means the clothes are attached to the impure person while they are impure, so they could be a special case.

phrases.english: for look, one who moved a carcass
makes clothes impure,
but does not make a person impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת's answer in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's rule that whatever makes clothes impure makes people impure.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A counter-case: one who moves a נבילה makes clothes impure but not people, so the rule does not always hold.

steps.title: Don't we learn שרץ the same way?
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת defends his rule: don't we know that a שרץ makes a person impure only because it makes clothes impure?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But then a שרץ, which makes a person impure, how do we know that? Is it not because it makes clothes impure?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת pushes back by saying his rule is already used elsewhere, for a שרץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rule 'clothes impure, so people impure' were wrong, we would have no source for שרץ making a person impure. רב ששת is trying to show the rule must be valid.

keyTerms.meaning: A dead creeping creature that makes things impure
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: He said to him:
But then a creeping creature, which makes a person impure:
from where do we know it?
Is it not because it makes clothes impure?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב ששת answers רב אחדבוי's objection with a counter-challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחדבוי's rejection of the rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without the rule, there would be no source for שרץ making a person impure.

steps.title: For שרץ, the פסוק says it openly
steps.stepSummary: רב אחדבוי answers that for a שרץ there is a clear פסוק, so the rule is not needed there.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: About a שרץ it is written openly: 'Or a man who touches any creeping creature.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחדבוי pushes aside רב ששת's proof: a שרץ making a person impure comes straight from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the תורה says it outright, the case of שרץ does not prove the rule 'clothes impure, so people impure'. רב ששת's support is gone.

phrases.english: He said to him:
With a creeping creature, it is written explicitly:
"Or a man who touches any creeping creature."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:5

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ששת's challenge from שרץ.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שרץ has its own explicit פסוק, so it does not show the rule is needed.

steps.title: Then what about שכבת זרע?
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת tries again: don't we learn that שכבת זרע makes a person impure from the fact that it makes clothes impure?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then שכבת זרע, which makes a person impure, how do we know that? Is it not because, since it makes clothes impure, it makes a person impure?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת brings a second case to show his rule is used: שכבת זרע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says clothes touched by שכבת זרע become impure. רב ששת argues the only source for a person becoming impure must be the same rule he used for the מצורע.

phrases.english: But then semen,
which makes a person impure: from where do we know it?
Is it not because, since it makes clothes impure,
it makes a person impure?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע דִּמְטַמֵּא אָדָם מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the שרץ proof fails, רב ששת tries a second case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחדבוי's rejection of the rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without the rule, there would be no source for שכבת זרע making a person impure.

steps.title: For שכבת זרע, the extra word 'or' teaches it
steps.stepSummary: רב אחדבוי answers that שכבת זרע also has its own source: the extra word 'or' in 'or a man' comes to include one who touches it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: About שכבת זרע it is also written openly: 'or a man', which comes to include one who touches it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחדבוי pushes aside the second proof as well: the טומאה of someone who touches שכבת זרע comes from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'או' is read as adding a new case: a person who touches שכבת זרע. So again the rule is not needed, and רב ששת's answer about the מצורע is left without support.

keyTerms.meaning: To include (an extra word adds a case)

steps.whatToRemember: רב ששת's rule ('clothes impure, so people impure') was challenged by היסט נבילה. Both of his supporting cases, שרץ and שכבת זרע, turned out to have their own פסוקים.

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע נָמֵי בְּהֶדְיָא כְּתִיב בֵּיהּ:
phrases.english: With semen too, it is written explicitly:
"Or a man":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:4. The word 'or' looks extra, so it is read as adding another case.

phrases.english: to include one who touches it.

steps.triggerLanguage: שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע נָמֵי בְּהֶדְיָא כְּתִיב בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ששת's challenge from שכבת זרע.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שכבת זרע has its own source in the extra word 'או', so it does not depend on the rule.

steps.title: רב אחדבוי's mocking tone and his punishment
steps.stepSummary: רב אחדבוי answered רב ששת mockingly. רב ששת was hurt, and רב אחדבוי lost his speech and forgot his learning.
steps.simpleTranslation: He answered him in a mocking way. רב ששת was hurt. רב אחדבוי בר אמי became mute and forgot his learning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the legal argument and tells a story about how it ended. רב אחדבוי's answers were said with mockery, and he was punished for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was not the content of his answers but the way he said them. He spoke as if רב ששת did not know the פסוקים. Hurting a great תלמיד חכם brought a heavy punishment: he lost his speech and his Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: in a joking or mocking way
his learning became 'heavy', meaning he forgot it

phrases.english: He answered him in a mocking way.
phrases.notes: This means רב אחדבוי, with each of his answers to רב ששת in the steps before.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet felt hurt.
Rav Achadvoi bar Ami became mute
and his learning was forgotten.
phrases.notes: Literally, 'his learning became heavy.' It felt too heavy to hold onto, so he forgot it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes the tone of רב אחדבוי's answers in steps 8 and 10 and what came of them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mocking a great Torah scholar brought severe punishment.

steps.title: His mother's plea and his healing
steps.stepSummary: רב אחדבוי's mother cried before רב ששת and reminded him that she had nursed him. He prayed, and רב אחדבוי was healed.
steps.simpleTranslation: His mother came and cried before רב ששת. She cried and cried, but he paid no attention. She said to him: Look at these breasts that you nursed from. He prayed for רב אחדבוי, and he was healed.
steps.whatsHappening: The story finishes. רב אחדבוי's mother reminds רב ששת of what she did for him as a baby, and he prays for her son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first רב ששת does not respond to her tears. Her reminder that she had nursed him is what moves him, and he prays for mercy and the punishment ends. This answers the question of step 3: רב אחדבוי's behavior drove his mother to act this way, so he was called 'the infant who perverted the ways of his mother.'

keyTerms.meaning: he paid no attention to her

phrases.english: His mother came and was crying before him.
She cried and cried, but he paid no attention to her.
She said to him:
Look at these breasts that you nursed from.
He prayed for mercy for him, and he was healed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story begun in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ששת's prayer, moved by gratitude to the woman who nursed him, healed רב אחדבוי.

steps.title: Asking for the source of the rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn the rule the story was about: a מצורע makes a person impure during his counting days.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the topic we came to: from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the legal question behind the story and asks for its source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת had tried to learn this rule from a general principle, and רב אחדבוי rejected that. So the גמרא now looks for a real source showing that a מצורע in his counting days makes a person impure.

keyTerms.meaning: and about the matter we came to
from where do we know this?

phrases.english: And about the matter we came to: from where do we know it?
phrases.notes: This means the rule from the earlier argument: a מצורע in his counting days makes a person impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and goes back to the legal topic of steps 4–10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a מצורע during his counting days makes a person impure.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן יוחי's גזירה שוה
steps.stepSummary: The same words, 'washing clothes,' appear for both the counting days and the confirmed days. So just as a confirmed מצורע makes a person impure, so does a מצורע in his counting days.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון בן יוחי says: 'Washing clothes' is said about his counting days, and 'washing clothes' is said about his days of confirmed צרעת. Just as there he makes a person impure, here too he makes a person impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. It links the two time periods of a מצורע through matching words in the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a גזירה שוה: the same phrase in two places teaches that the two cases share a law. A confirmed מצורע clearly makes a person impure. Because 'washing clothes' appears in both places, a מצורע in his counting days does too. This gives the real source that רב אחדבוי was looking for.

keyTerms.meaning: his days of confirmed צרעת, after the כהן declares him definitely impure
learning one case from another because of matching words in the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: A מצורע makes people impure even during his counting days. We learn this from a גזירה שוה on the words 'washing clothes,' not from רב ששת's general rule.

phrases.aramaic: כִּדְתַנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says:
'Washing clothes' is said about his counting days,
and 'washing clothes' is said about his days of confirmed tzaraas.
Just as there, he makes a person impure,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the confirmed days, where it is clear he makes a person impure.

phrases.english: so too here, he makes a person impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְתַנְיָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה from 'washing clothes' links the counting days to the confirmed days, so in both a מצורע makes a person impure.

steps.title: Secret צדקה is greater than משה רבינו
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says a person who gives צדקה in secret is greater than משה רבינו. משה feared God's anger and wrath, but secret giving calms both.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: One who gives צדקה in secret is greater than משה רבינו. About משה רבינו it is written: 'For I was afraid of the anger and the wrath.' But about one who gives צדקה it is written: 'A gift in secret calms anger, and a present in the bosom, fierce wrath.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its earlier topic of צדקה. רבי אלעזר compares a secret giver to משה רבינו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה said he was afraid of אף and חמה, two kinds of divine anger. The פסוק in משלי says secret giving calms אף and also חמה. So the secret giver can calm what even משה feared.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Great is one who gives charity in secret,
more than Moshe our teacher.
For about Moshe our teacher it is written:
"For I was afraid of the anger and the wrath,"
phrases.notes: דברים 9:19

phrases.english: while about one who gives charity it is written:
"A gift in secret calms anger,
phrases.notes: משלי 21:14

phrases.english: and a present in the bosom, fierce wrath."
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording to finish the פסוק. This second half is the part that mentions חמה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר גָּדוֹל הָעוֹשֶׂה צְדָקָה בַּסֵּתֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section, going back to the praise of צדקה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Secret צדקה calms both אף and חמה, which even משה feared.

steps.title: רבי יצחק disagrees: secret giving does not calm wrath
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי יצחק disagrees. He reads the פסוק to mean secret giving calms אף but not חמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This disagrees with רבי יצחק, for רבי יצחק said: It calms anger, but it does not calm wrath. As it says: 'And a present in the bosom, fierce wrath.' Even though the present is in the bosom, there is still fierce wrath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבי יצחק reads the same פסוק differently from רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר read the second half as 'a present in the bosom calms fierce wrath.' רבי יצחק reads it as 'even with a secret present, fierce wrath remains.' On his reading, the secret giver is not greater than משה on this point.

keyTerms.meaning: a present hidden in the bosom, meaning given secretly

steps.confusionAlert: Both רבי אלעזר and רבי יצחק read the same פסוק. They split over its second half: does the secret gift calm fierce wrath, or does fierce wrath remain even so?

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rabbi Yitzchak,
for Rabbi Yitzchak said:
It calms anger, but it does not calm wrath,
as it says: "And a present in the bosom, fierce wrath":
even though the present is in the bosom,
there is still fierce wrath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows an opinion that argues with רבי אלעזר in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Secret giving calms אף, but fierce חמה remains.

steps.title: Another version: a judge who takes a bribe
steps.stepSummary: Some report רבי יצחק differently: the פסוק is about a judge who takes a bribe and brings fierce wrath on the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say that רבי יצחק said: Any judge who takes a bribe brings fierce wrath to the world, as it says: 'And a present in the bosom...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of what רבי יצחק said about the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, שחד means an actual bribe, not צדקה. A judge who takes one brings fierce wrath. In this version רבי יצחק is not talking about צדקה at all, so he does not argue with רבי אלעזר about it.

phrases.english: Some say that Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Any judge who takes a bribe
brings fierce wrath to the world,
as it says: "And a present in the bosom," and so on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another version of רבי יצחק's statement from step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A judge who takes a bribe brings fierce wrath to the world.

steps.title: Six blessings for giving, eleven for comforting
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק teaches: giving a פרוטה to a poor person earns six blessings, and comforting him with words earns eleven.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק said: Anyone who gives a פרוטה to a poor person is blessed with six blessings. One who comforts him with words is blessed with eleven blessings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching of רבי יצחק about helping the poor. This sets up the next step, where the sources are shown.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A small coin brings six blessings. Kind, encouraging words bring even more: eleven. This shows how much warmth and caring toward the poor are worth.

keyTerms.meaning: one who comforts him with words

steps.whyThisMatters: Kind words to a poor person are counted as even greater than giving money.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Anyone who gives a perutah to a poor person
is blessed with six blessings,
and one who comforts him with words
is blessed with eleven blessings.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק כׇּל הַנּוֹתֵן פְּרוּטָה לְעָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching by the same רבי יצחק, still on the topic of צדקה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Giving a פרוטה brings six blessings; comforting the poor with words brings eleven.

steps.title: The source for the six blessings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows the source for the six blessings: the פסוק in ישעיהו about sharing bread, bringing the poor home, and clothing the naked.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who gives a פרוטה to a poor person is blessed with six blessings, as it is written: 'Is it not to share your bread... and bring the poor who are cast out into your house... when you see the naked...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins proving the first half of רבי יצחק's teaching from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists acts of giving to the poor. The פסוקים right after it list the rewards, which come to six blessings. The גמרא quotes only the start and expects us to know the rest.

keyTerms.meaning: to share, to break bread for others
poor people who are cast out, homeless

phrases.english: One who gives a perutah to a poor person
is blessed with six blessings,
as it is written: "Is it not to share," and so on,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 58:7

phrases.english: "and bring the poor who are cast out into your house,"
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some don't.

phrases.english: "when you see the naked," and so on.
phrases.notes: The six blessings themselves come in the next פסוקים, ישעיהו 58:8–9.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַנּוֹתֵן פְּרוּטָה לְעָנִי מִתְבָּרֵךְ בְּשֵׁשׁ בְּרָכוֹת דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts proving the six blessings mentioned in step 18.
steps.raayaObject: The six blessings for giving a פרוטה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 58:7, together with the blessings in the פסוקים that follow.

steps.title: The source for the eleven blessings for comforting a poor person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the פסוקים in ישעיהו that list eleven blessings for someone who comforts a poor person with words.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one who comforts the poor person with words gets eleven blessings, because the פסוק says: 'If you draw out your soul to the hungry and satisfy the suffering soul, your light will shine in the darkness and your gloom will be like noon. ה׳ will guide you always and satisfy your soul in dry places... and those from you will build the ancient ruins; you will raise up the foundations of many generations...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing רבי יצחק's teaching from step 18 by giving the proof for the eleven blessings. It brings the פסוקים that come right after the ones about the six blessings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 19, the six blessings came from פסוקים about physically giving food, shelter, and clothing. Here the פסוק talks about 'drawing out your soul' to the hungry, meaning reaching out to him with feeling and kind words. Those פסוקים list even more blessings, so comforting is rewarded more than giving money alone.

keyTerms.meaning: one who comforts him, calming and encouraging a poor person
'and you draw out your soul to the hungry,' meaning you reach out to him with real feeling
'and so on,' meaning the פסוק continues

steps.whatToRemember: Giving a פרוטה earns six blessings, but comforting a poor person with words earns eleven. Kind words count for even more than money.

phrases.english: And one who comforts him with words
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the poor person from רבי יצחק's teaching in step 18.

phrases.english: is blessed with eleven blessings
as it is said: "And if you draw out your soul to the hungry
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 58:10–12

then your light shall shine in the darkness
and your gloom shall be like noon.
And ה׳ will guide you always,
and satisfy your soul in dry places, and so on,
and those who come from you will build the ancient ruins,
you will raise up the foundations of many generations, and so on."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the source for the second half of רבי יצחק's statement. Step 19 proved the six blessings; this step proves the eleven.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that comforting a poor person with words earns eleven blessings
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 58:10–12, which lists many blessings for 'drawing out your soul' to the hungry

steps.title: One who chases after צדקה is given money to give
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק explains a פסוק in משלי: the reward for pursuing צדקה is not becoming poor yourself. It is that הקב״ה provides you with money so you can keep giving.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: What does the פסוק mean, 'One who pursues צדקה and kindness will find life, צדקה, and honor'? Is it saying that because he chased after צדקה, he himself will end up receiving צדקה?! Rather, it teaches that anyone who pursues צדקה, הקב״ה provides him with money so he can do צדקה with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק asks about a strange-sounding פסוק and then explains it. The פסוק seems to say the giver's reward is to 'find צדקה,' which sounds like he will need it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, 'he will find צדקה' would mean the giver becomes poor and others give to him, which would be a terrible reward. רבי יצחק rejects that reading. Instead, 'finding צדקה' means finding the money to give more צדקה: הקב״ה keeps supplying him so he can keep giving.

keyTerms.meaning: one who pursues צדקה, chasing after chances to give
what is meant by what is written? This opens an explanation of a פסוק
rather, it comes to tell you. This introduces the real meaning

steps.confusionAlert: The question 'משום דרודף צדקה ימצא צדקה?!' is not a question from the outside. It is רבי יצחק pointing out why the simple reading cannot be right, so he can give the correct one.

phrases.english: And רבי יצחק said:
What is meant by what is written:
"One who pursues charity and kindness
will find life, charity, and honor"?
phrases.notes: משלי 21:21

phrases.english: Because he pursues charity,
he will find charity?!
phrases.notes: He means: would the giver's reward really be that he becomes poor and needs charity himself?

phrases.english: Rather, it is to tell you:
Anyone who pursues charity,

phrases.aramaic: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַמְצִיא לוֹ מָעוֹת
phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, provides him with money
and he does charity with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching from רבי יצחק about צדקה, this time explaining a פסוק in משלי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who pursues צדקה is given money by הקב״ה so he can keep giving.

steps.title: הקב״ה sends worthy people to the one who gives
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains the פסוק differently: הקב״ה sends the giver worthy recipients so that he earns full reward.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: הקב״ה provides him with worthy people to give צדקה to, so that he will receive reward for helping them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives his own explanation of 'he will find צדקה' from the פסוק in משלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יצחק, the giver 'finds' money to give. For רב נחמן בר יצחק, the giver 'finds' the right people to give to. Giving to someone who doesn't really deserve it brings less reward, so being sent worthy people is a real blessing.

keyTerms.meaning: worthy, deserving people who truly need the help
to receive his reward for them

phrases.english: רב נחמן בר יצחק said:
The Holy One, Blessed be He, provides him
with people who are worthy
to give charity to them,
so that he receives his reward for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second explanation of the same פסוק that רבי יצחק explained in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who pursues צדקה is sent worthy recipients so that he gets full reward.

steps.title: What idea is רב נחמן בר יצחק pushing away?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which other idea רב נחמן בר יצחק's teaching comes to exclude.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does this come to exclude?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the next step: what opposite idea is רב נחמן בר יצחק's statement pushing aside?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'הקב״ה sends worthy people' suggests that sometimes the opposite happens, and a person gets sent unworthy people. The גמרא wants to know where that opposite idea comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: to exclude what? It asks which other idea a statement is ruling out

phrases.english: To exclude what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the purpose of רב נחמן בר יצחק's statement in step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which opposite situation רב נחמן בר יצחק's statement is meant to exclude

steps.title: ירמיה's prayer that his enemies give to unworthy people
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב נחמן בר יצחק's teaching excludes the situation רבה described. ירמיה prayed that even when his enemies give צדקה, they should be sent unworthy people so they get no reward.
steps.simpleTranslation: It excludes what רבה taught. רבה explained the פסוק 'Let them be made to stumble before You; deal with them in the time of Your anger.' ירמיה said to הקב״ה: Master of the world, even when they overpower their evil inclination and want to give צדקה before You, make them stumble onto unworthy people, so that they will not get reward for helping them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 23. רב נחמן בר יצחק's teaching is the opposite of the curse ירמיה placed on his enemies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה shows that being sent unworthy recipients can be a punishment, since it takes away the reward of the giving. A good person who pursues צדקה gets the reverse: הקב״ה makes sure he finds worthy people. So רב נחמן בר יצחק is telling us the righteous giver is spared what ירמיה asked for against the wicked.

keyTerms.meaning: רבה expounded, explaining the deeper meaning of a פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: Finding worthy people to give to is a reward in itself. Being sent unworthy people can be a punishment that takes away the merit of giving.

phrases.english: To exclude what רבה expounded,
for רבה expounded:
What is meant by what is written:
"Let them be made to stumble before You;
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 18:23

phrases.english: deal with them in the time of Your anger"?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר יִרְמְיָה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: ירמיה said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the world,
[even] at the time that they overpower their evil inclination
phrases.notes: 'They' are the people ירמיה is praying against in this פסוק. The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: and want to give charity before You,
make them stumble onto people who are not worthy,
so that they will not receive reward for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23 by naming the opposite idea: רבה's explanation of ירמיה's prayer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב נחמן בר יצחק's teaching excludes the fate ירמיה asked for his enemies: being sent unworthy recipients so their צדקה earns no reward.

steps.title: Regular givers of צדקה merit wise, wealthy, and learned children
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that one who regularly gives צדקה merits sons who are masters of wisdom, wealth, and אגדה. The גמרא begins bringing a source for each.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Anyone who regularly gives צדקה merits to have sons who are masters of wisdom, masters of wealth, and masters of אגדה. Masters of wisdom, as it is written:
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי gives a new reward for giving צדקה regularly: special children. At the end, the גמרא sets up the proof for the first of the three, 'masters of wisdom,' and the פסוק comes on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key word is 'רגיל,' meaning someone who gives as a steady habit, not just once. The reward is three kinds of children: wise, wealthy, and skilled in אגדה. The words 'בעלי חכמה – דכתיב' open a list of proofs for each of the three.

keyTerms.meaning: one who is used to doing something, a person who does it as a habit
masters of אגדה, the stories and teachings of the תורה beyond strict הלכה

phrases.english: רבי יהושע בן לוי said:
Anyone who regularly gives charity
merits to have sons

phrases.aramaic: בַּעֲלֵי חׇכְמָה, בַּעֲלֵי עוֹשֶׁר, בַּעֲלֵי אַגָּדָה.
phrases.english: who are masters of wisdom, masters of wealth, and masters of אגדה.
Masters of wisdom, as it is written:
phrases.notes: The פסוק itself comes right after this, on the next עמוד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching about the rewards of צדקה, moving from finding money and worthy recipients to blessings in one's children.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who regularly gives צדקה merits sons who are masters of wisdom, wealth, and אגדה.
